text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore government reduces economic growth forecast to about 6 percent for this year as third quarter slows down to 3.2 percent, and expects growth for 1997 to be between 5 and 7 percent.
- Pakistan Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto sacked, for second time in her political career, by country's president for corruption, nepotism amd misrule.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says visit to cambodia brings back memories of Singapore in 1960s and highlights lesson that small countries could not take prosperity for granted.
- Baring Futures' auditor seeks to halt Singapore $2 billion negligence lawsuit.
- Census of Real Estate & Business Services records says that lawyers maintain the lion's share of business services sector earnings in 1994 of Singapore $304.3 million.
- Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says Singapore government will not need to make any drastic policy adjustments to cope with current economic slowdown.
- Impending bankruptcy of leading Japanese property development, Osaka-based Sueno Kosan, sends shockwaves through Tokyo financial markets.
- Final polls give U.S. President Bill Clinton lead by 11 percentage points.
- Liem Sioe Liong's Salim group, Usman Admadjaja's Danamon International and Nusamba buys 15.6 percent of PT Astra International for 736.7 billion rupiah.
- Tongkah Holdings Bhd says it agrees to purchase additional shares in Hospital Pantai Bhd, up to 21 percent from 4.5 percent.
- Computer Systems Advisers (M) Sdn Bhd, subsidiary of CSA Holdings, awaits approval from Malaysia's Securities Commission for listing on second board of Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
- Straits Steamship Land emerges as fourth party in Cockpit hotel redevelopment project.
- Malayan Credit Ltd pays Singapore $94 million for five Grange Garden sites.
